reasons.A: Long, clause-heavy sentences joined by semicolons, steady hedging ('it seems to me', 'I suspect', 'in some sense'), a reader aside and few paragraphs match the passage's measured, reflective movement most closely, though it leans a little on the hedges.
reasons.B: Flowing sentences with semicolons, a calm explanatory stance and no contractions are close to the author, but it hedges less and breaks into more short declaratives than the passage does.
reasons.D: It has the author's hedges and a rhetorical question, but the clipped sentences ('It rarely does.'), short paragraphs and the one-line epigram close make it more punchy and aphoristic than the passage.
reasons.C: Short, plain sentences, contractions ('won't', 'isn't'), second-person advice and many small paragraphs read as a brisk modern business voice, far from the author's long, hedged periodic sentences.
